questions.question: A small network has up to about:
questions.explanation: A small network serves up to about 200 devices.

questions.question: A large network has:
questions.explanation: A large network has more than 1,000 devices.

questions.question: Which design principle breaks the complex network design problem into smaller, manageable areas?
questions.explanation: Hierarchy divides the design into layers, so each area is smaller and easier to manage.

questions.question: Which layer is the backbone of the hierarchical network?
questions.explanation: The core layer is the high-speed backbone of the hierarchical network.

questions.question: The access layer is where:

options.A: End devices and local servers connect to the network

questions.explanation: The access layer is the point where end devices and local servers attach to the network.

questions.question: The distribution layer is also called the:
questions.explanation: The distribution layer is also known as the workgroup layer.

questions.question: The access layer is also called the:
questions.explanation: The access layer is also known as the workstation layer.

questions.question: Which layer is the boundary between Layer 2 and Layer 3?
questions.explanation: The distribution layer marks the boundary between the Layer 2 access network and the Layer 3 core.

questions.question: Power over Ethernet (PoE) supplies power to devices through the:
questions.explanation: PoE delivers power to devices over the same network cable that carries data.

questions.question: Port security controls:

options.A: Which devices can use a port

questions.explanation: Port security restricts which devices are allowed to use a switch port.

questions.question: The main purpose of the core layer is:
questions.explanation: The core layer exists to switch packets at high speed.

questions.question: A flat network design is mainly used today for:
questions.explanation: A flat design suits only very small networks.

questions.question: An enterprise network is the IT infrastructure that:

options.A: Connects users, devices and applications in midsize and large organizations

questions.explanation: An enterprise network connects users, devices and applications across midsize and large organizations.

questions.question: In a two-tier design, the core is collapsed into the:
questions.explanation: In a two-tier design, the core and distribution functions are combined in the distribution layer.

questions.question: A three-tier design is recommended when:

options.B: The network is a single room
options.D: More than two pairs of distribution switches are required

questions.explanation: A separate core is justified when more than two pairs of distribution switches must be connected.

questions.question: Traffic between servers within a data center is called:
questions.explanation: Server-to-server traffic inside a data center is called east-west traffic.

questions.question: Traffic between endpoints and the WAN edge, Internet or data center is called:
questions.explanation: Traffic between endpoints and the WAN edge, Internet or data center is north-south traffic.

questions.question: The Internet of Things (IoT) is a combination of:
questions.explanation: IoT combines sensors that collect data with actuators that act on it.

questions.question: High availability means a system can operate:
questions.explanation: High availability means the system keeps running continuously with minimal downtime.

questions.question: The IoT architecture is divided into how many layers?
questions.explanation: The IoT architecture has four layers.

questions.question: High-availability clusters are also known as:
questions.explanation: HA clusters are also called failover clusters.

questions.question: Failover means:

options.D: A failed primary component's work moves to a backup component

questions.explanation: Failover transfers the work of a failed primary component to a backup component.

questions.question: A heartbeat program is used to:

options.C: Send packets to confirm each cluster node is working

questions.explanation: A heartbeat program sends packets to confirm that each cluster node is still working.

questions.question: Cloud networking uses:

options.B: Cloud-based services to deploy a corporate network

questions.explanation: Cloud networking uses cloud-based services to deploy a corporate network.

questions.question: Fault tolerance aims for:
questions.explanation: Fault tolerance aims for zero downtime.

questions.question: Which is more expensive?
questions.explanation: Fault tolerance needs duplicate physical components, so it is more expensive than high availability.

questions.question: In Cisco's troubleshooting method, which layer should you check first?
questions.explanation: Cisco's method starts at the physical layer, since cables and ports are the most basic cause of faults.

questions.question: The top-down approach starts from the:
questions.explanation: The top-down approach begins at the application layer and works downwards.

questions.question: The bottom-up approach starts from the:
questions.explanation: The bottom-up approach begins at the physical layer and works upwards.

questions.question: The divide and conquer approach usually starts at the:
questions.explanation: Divide and conquer usually starts at the transport layer and moves up or down depending on the result.

questions.question: The ping command uses which protocol?
questions.explanation: Ping uses ICMP echo request and echo reply messages.

questions.question: ARP links:

options.A: An IP address to a MAC address
options.B: A domain name to an IP

questions.explanation: ARP resolves an IP address to a MAC address.

questions.question: Traceroute shows:

options.B: The path and where the packet stops

questions.explanation: Traceroute lists each hop on the path, showing where the packet stops.

questions.question: The route command is used to:
questions.explanation: The route command lets you view and manually update the routing table.

questions.question: Telnet provides:

options.C: A command-line interface to a remote device

questions.explanation: Telnet gives a command-line interface to a remote device.

questions.question: A duplicate IP address problem can be fixed in Windows using:
questions.explanation: Releasing and renewing the lease with ipconfig /release and /renew obtains a fresh address.

questions.question: nslookup shows the:

options.A: Domain name to IP address mapping

questions.explanation: nslookup queries DNS and shows the domain name to IP address mapping.

questions.question: Cloud networking lets a third-party provider:

options.D: Manage and maintain the networking hardware and infrastructure

questions.explanation: With cloud networking, the provider manages and maintains the networking hardware and infrastructure.

questions.question: Network virtualization is the:

options.A: Replacement of all software with hardware

questions.explanation: Network virtualization implements networking services in software.

questions.question: A Bluetooth network is an example of an:
questions.explanation: Bluetooth devices connect directly without an access point, which is an ad hoc network.

questions.question: NFV replaces physical network devices with:

options.A: Virtual services that perform the same functions

questions.explanation: Network Functions Virtualization replaces physical devices with virtual services doing the same job.

questions.question: How many channels does Bluetooth hop among?
questions.explanation: Bluetooth hops among 79 channels.

questions.question: Bluetooth uses which spread spectrum technique?
questions.explanation: Bluetooth uses frequency hopping spread spectrum (FHSS).

questions.question: 802.11a works in which frequency band?
questions.explanation: 802.11a operates in the 5 GHz band.

questions.question: 802.11n supports:
questions.explanation: 802.11n introduced MIMO, using multiple antennas.

questions.question: The multiple access technique used by 802.11 is:
questions.explanation: Wi-Fi uses CSMA/CA, because wireless stations cannot reliably detect collisions.

questions.question: A vNIC allows a virtual machine to:
questions.explanation: A virtual NIC gives a virtual machine access to a network.

questions.question: WEP uses which stream cipher?
questions.explanation: WEP encrypts with the RC4 stream cipher.

questions.question: WPA2 uses which cipher?
questions.explanation: WPA2 uses the AES-CCMP cipher.

questions.question: Which is the newest Wi-Fi security protocol among these?
questions.explanation: WPA3 is the newest of the four.

questions.question: Resiliency in network design means the network:

options.C: Remains available under normal and abnormal conditions such as failures and DoS events

questions.explanation: A resilient network stays available under normal and abnormal conditions, including failures and DoS events.

questions.question: Flexibility in network design means the ability to:

options.A: Change parts of the network, add services or increase capacity without major changes

questions.explanation: Flexibility means the network can be modified, extended or scaled without major redesign.

questions.question: What is a drawback of a flat network as it grows?

options.D: Response time becomes slow and management becomes difficult

questions.explanation: As a flat network grows, response time slows and management becomes difficult.

questions.question: Which is a benefit of hierarchical design?

options.A: All traffic goes to the core

questions.explanation: Hierarchical design keeps local traffic local instead of sending everything to the core.

questions.question: Which is a function of the access layer?

options.D: Port security, PoE, QoS classification and ARP inspection

questions.explanation: The access layer provides port security, PoE, QoS classification and ARP inspection.

questions.question: What is the purpose of an auxiliary VLAN in the access layer?

options.C: A separate VLAN for voice (VoIP) traffic

questions.explanation: An auxiliary VLAN carries voice (VoIP) traffic separately from data traffic.

questions.question: The distribution layer acts as the demarcation point between:
questions.explanation: The distribution layer separates broadcast domains, forming the boundary between the access and core layers.

questions.question: Routing between routing domains, such as EIGRP to OSPF, is a function of the:
questions.explanation: The distribution layer handles routing between different routing domains.

questions.question: The core layer scales by:
questions.explanation: The core is kept simple and scales by using faster devices.

questions.question: A collapsed core (two-tier) design is cost-effective because:

options.A: There are no separate core layer devices

questions.explanation: In a collapsed core design, the distribution layer also acts as the core, so no separate core devices are needed.

questions.question: Which block is used for regular Internet access, e-commerce and remote VPN access?
questions.explanation: The Internet Edge block provides Internet access, e-commerce and remote VPN access.

questions.question: The WAN Edge block connects to:

options.B: Remote data centers, remote branches, other campuses or cloud providers

questions.explanation: The WAN Edge block connects the enterprise to remote data centers, branches, other campuses and cloud providers.

questions.question: Why might a large campus choose a three-tier design?

options.B: Multiple buildings need a dedicated distribution layer

questions.explanation: Multiple buildings need a dedicated distribution layer and a core to interconnect them.

questions.question: Which design is more suitable for east-west traffic in a data center?
questions.explanation: A leaf-spine design gives short, predictable paths between servers, which suits east-west traffic.

questions.question: HA cluster nodes typically share the same:
questions.explanation: The nodes of an HA cluster typically share the same storage.

questions.question: At the application layer, which software is critical for application availability?
questions.explanation: Load-balancing software spreads requests across servers and keeps the application available.

questions.question: Replication in HA means:

options.A: Data is replicated and shared so any node can step in when another fails

questions.explanation: Replication copies and shares data so another node can take over when one fails.

questions.question: A best practice for failover systems is to locate them:
questions.explanation: Placing failover systems off-premises protects them from a site-wide failure that affects the primary.

questions.question: Compared with fault tolerance, high availability is:

options.C: Less expensive, as it does not need duplicate physical components

questions.explanation: High availability does not need duplicate physical components, so it costs less.

questions.question: Fault tolerance mainly focuses on:

options.B: Preventing mission-critical applications from experiencing downtime

questions.explanation: Fault tolerance is about preventing mission-critical applications from experiencing downtime.

questions.question: "Make no assumptions" in Cisco's methodology means you should:

options.B: See for yourself what the cause is

questions.explanation: It means verifying the cause yourself instead of assuming.

questions.question: Documenting troubleshooting steps helps to:

options.A: Avoid repeating work and allow rollback of changes

questions.explanation: Documented steps avoid repeated work and allow changes to be rolled back.

questions.question: The top-down method is best when:

options.D: The problem seems related to an application

questions.explanation: Top-down suits problems that appear to involve an application.

questions.question: The divide and conquer method is useful when:

options.A: The cause is a cut cable
options.B: The cause is clearly an application bug
options.C: You have no clear idea of the cause
options.D: You already know the root cause

questions.explanation: Divide and conquer helps when you have no clear idea of the cause, since you start in the middle and narrow it down.

questions.question: In cloud networking, a third-party provider manages the networking hardware so administrators can focus on:
questions.explanation: With hardware handled by the provider, administrators can focus on efficiency and optimizing configuration.

questions.question: In a traceroute output, the first column shows the:
questions.explanation: The first column of traceroute output is the hop number.

questions.question: In traceroute, the same routers appearing again and again indicates a:
questions.explanation: Repeating routers show packets circulating between routers, which is a routing loop.

questions.question: A successful ping shows:

options.D: Replies with round-trip time and 0% loss

questions.explanation: A successful ping returns replies with round-trip times and 0% packet loss.

questions.question: IP address exhaustion means:

options.A: The IP address is too long
options.D: The DHCP server is out of addresses or the request never reached it

questions.explanation: IP exhaustion occurs when the DHCP server has no addresses left, or the request never reaches it.

questions.question: Common causes of Wi-Fi problems include:
questions.explanation: Wi-Fi problems commonly come from congestion, distance and interference.

questions.question: To fix a "DNS Name Does Not Exist" error, you can:

options.B: Obtain DNS automatically, flush the DNS cache or change the DNS server

questions.explanation: The error is addressed by obtaining DNS automatically, flushing the DNS cache or changing the DNS server.

questions.question: "Non-authoritative answer" in nslookup means the data:

options.A: Came from a cache or another DNS server, not the authoritative source

questions.explanation: A non-authoritative answer comes from a cache or another DNS server instead of the authoritative source.

questions.question: In an infrastructure WLAN, a client:

options.B: Associates with all WAPs at once
options.C: Authenticates and then associates with only one WAP at a time

questions.explanation: A client authenticates and then associates with only one WAP at a time.

questions.question: Roaming happens when:

options.D: A client goes out of range of one WAP and associates with another

questions.explanation: Roaming is a client moving out of range of one WAP and associating with another.

questions.question: Bluetooth uses time slots of:
questions.explanation: Bluetooth time slots are 625 microseconds long.

questions.question: Which is the correct difference between Bluetooth and Ethernet?

options.B: Bluetooth is wireless (PAN); Ethernet is wired (LAN)
options.C: Ethernet is wireless; Bluetooth is wired

questions.explanation: Bluetooth is a wireless personal area network, while Ethernet is a wired LAN.

questions.question: 802.11g uses OFDM and has a maximum rate of:
questions.explanation: 802.11g uses OFDM with a maximum rate of 54 Mbps.

questions.question: 802.11b operates at 2.4 GHz and has a maximum rate of:
questions.explanation: 802.11b reaches a maximum of 11 Mbps.

questions.question: 802.11ac (Wi-Fi 5) operates in:
questions.explanation: 802.11ac works in the 5 GHz band with up to 3.47 Gbps.

questions.question: 802.11ax is also known as:
questions.explanation: 802.11ax is marketed as Wi-Fi 6.

questions.question: MAC ID filtering allows access only to:

options.C: Devices whose MAC address is in the approved list

questions.explanation: MAC filtering admits only devices whose MAC addresses are on the approved list.

questions.question: WEP is insecure because it:

options.D: Uses a small static key with the RC4 cipher

questions.explanation: WEP's small static key and RC4 cipher make it easy to break.

questions.question: TKIP improves WEP by:

options.A: Sending a different key with each packet

questions.explanation: TKIP uses a different key for each packet.

questions.question: EAP-TLS is used with:
questions.explanation: EAP-TLS is an authentication method used with WPA2-Enterprise.

questions.question: WPA and WPA2 are based on which IEEE standard?
questions.explanation: WPA and WPA2 are based on the IEEE 802.11i standard.

questions.question: WPA uses TKIP while WPA2 uses:
questions.explanation: WPA2 replaces TKIP with AES-CCMP.

questions.question: WPA3 was released in:
questions.explanation: WPA3 was released in 2018.

questions.question: In the IoT architecture, the object sensing layer:

options.A: Collects data using sensors attached to objects

questions.explanation: The object sensing layer collects data through sensors attached to objects.

questions.question: In cloud networking, virtualization lets you define:

options.A: Virtual routers, virtual firewalls and virtual load balancers in software

questions.explanation: Virtualization allows routers, firewalls and load balancers to be defined in software.

questions.question: A virtual switch (vSwitch) in VMware:

options.B: Sends traffic between its attached port groups and other network ports

questions.explanation: A vSwitch forwards traffic between its attached port groups and other network ports.

questions.question: Which statement correctly compares high availability (HA) and fault tolerance (FT)?

options.A: HA aims for zero downtime and is costlier; FT aims for minimal downtime and is cheaper
options.B: HA aims for minimal downtime and is cheaper; FT aims for zero downtime and is costlier
options.D: HA needs fully duplicate systems; FT needs none

questions.explanation: HA targets minimal downtime at lower cost, while FT targets zero downtime at higher cost.

questions.question: Which function is NOT performed by the access layer?

options.D: Routing between routing domains such as EIGRP to OSPF

questions.explanation: Routing between routing domains is a distribution layer function, not an access layer one.

questions.question: Which functions belong to the distribution layer?

options.A: Aggregation of LAN/WAN links and policy-based security using ACLs

questions.explanation: The distribution layer aggregates LAN/WAN links and applies policy-based security such as ACLs.

questions.question: Which is NOT a function of the core layer?
questions.explanation: Port security for end devices belongs to the access layer, not the core.

questions.question: A network serving about 700 devices is classified as a:
questions.explanation: A network with 200 to 1,000 devices is medium-size, so 700 devices fits that class.

questions.question: Why must future scale, expansion and manageability be considered before choosing a two-tier design?

options.A: The collapsed core may limit growth later
options.C: Two-tier designs are always more expensive

questions.explanation: The collapsed core can become a limit as the network grows.

questions.question: Which is a reason to choose a three-tier design?

options.A: The network has a single floor
options.B: The network has fewer than 10 users
options.C: Geographic dispersion of access switches needs more fibre than one collapsed core can support

questions.explanation: When access switches are widely dispersed and need more fibre than a collapsed core can support, a separate core is needed.

questions.question: Why does the data center block in the PPT use a leaf-spine design?

options.B: To handle east-west traffic between servers

questions.explanation: Leaf-spine suits the heavy east-west traffic between servers in a data center.

questions.question: Which statement about north-south traffic is correct?

options.A: It flows only between servers in a data center
options.B: It flows only between two switches
options.C: It never leaves the access layer
options.D: It flows between endpoints and the WAN edge, data center, Internet or network services blocks

questions.explanation: North-south traffic flows between endpoints and the WAN edge, data center, Internet or network services blocks.

questions.question: In an HA cluster, if one node fails:

options.A: Another node takes over immediately, so there is no single point of failure

questions.explanation: Another node takes over, so the cluster has no single point of failure.

questions.question: Which set lists the usual features of HA software?

options.B: Load balancing and redirecting, automatic failover, real-time file replication and automatic failback

questions.explanation: HA software typically offers load balancing and redirecting, automatic failover, real-time file replication and automatic failback.

questions.question: Which HA element means data is shared among nodes so any one can step in?
questions.explanation: Replication shares data among nodes so any of them can take over.

questions.question: Fault tolerance is best defined as a system's ability to:

options.A: Keep operating without interruption even if multiple components fail

questions.explanation: Fault tolerance means continuing to operate without interruption even when components fail.

questions.question: Which troubleshooting approach is best if a physical or connectivity problem is suspected?
questions.explanation: Bottom-up starts at the physical layer, so it fits suspected physical or connectivity problems.

questions.question: Divide and conquer typically uses which tools starting at the Transport layer?
questions.explanation: Divide and conquer typically uses ping and traceroute to test connectivity from the Transport layer.

questions.question: Ping reports "Request timed out" and traceroute stops after hop 3 with * * *. What does this suggest?

options.B: The problem is at or after the last working hop
options.D: The NIC is disabled on hop 1

questions.explanation: Traceroute stopping after hop 3 means the problem is at or after the last working hop.

questions.question: Which statement is correct?

options.A: Ping tests reachability and gives round-trip time; traceroute shows where the path breaks
options.B: Ping shows the path; traceroute shows only the RTT

questions.explanation: Ping checks reachability and RTT, and traceroute shows the path and where it breaks.

questions.question: Two devices on the same network have the same IP address. The best fix is to:

options.D: Release and renew the IP address

questions.explanation: Releasing and renewing the address gets a unique address from DHCP.

questions.question: When a PC cannot get an IP address, which step helps find if DHCP requests reach the server?

options.B: Check the VLAN of the port and whether other devices in that VLAN can get an IP

questions.explanation: Checking the port's VLAN and whether other devices in it get an IP shows if DHCP requests are reaching the server.

questions.question: In nslookup output, "Server: dns.google, Address: 8.8.8.8" tells you:

options.C: Which DNS server performed the lookup

questions.explanation: This line identifies the DNS server that answered the query.

questions.question: Which statement about an infrastructure WLAN is correct?

options.B: A client associates with all WAPs together
options.C: It is the same as Bluetooth
options.D: A client associates with only one WAP at a time

questions.explanation: In an infrastructure WLAN a client associates with only one WAP at a time.

questions.question: Which pair correctly matches wireless types?

options.A: Infrastructure - uses WAPs; Ad hoc - no WAP (for example, Bluetooth)
options.B: Infrastructure - no WAP; Ad hoc - uses WAPs

questions.explanation: Infrastructure networks use WAPs, while ad hoc networks such as Bluetooth do not.

questions.question: Bluetooth resists interference because:

options.C: It hops among 79 channels in a pseudo-random manner (FHSS)

questions.explanation: Frequency hopping across 79 channels helps Bluetooth avoid interference.

questions.question: Which describes 802.11a?

options.B: 5 GHz, 54 Mbps maximum, about 20 Mbps usable, short range

questions.explanation: 802.11a uses 5 GHz, has a 54 Mbps maximum with about 20 Mbps usable, and has short range.

questions.question: The usable speed of 802.11g (54 Mbps maximum) is about:
questions.explanation: The usable speed of 802.11g is about 22 Mbps.

questions.question: Which describes 802.11n?

options.A: 5 GHz only with OFDM and 54 Mbps
options.D: 40 MHz bandwidth with MIMO and 600 Mbps theoretical speed

questions.explanation: 802.11n uses 40 MHz channels with MIMO for a theoretical speed of 600 Mbps.

questions.question: 802.11af operates in:

options.B: Unused TV bands with about 1 km range

questions.explanation: 802.11af uses unused TV bands and has a range of about 1 km.

questions.question: 802.11ah operates at:
questions.explanation: 802.11ah operates at 900 MHz with a range of about 1 km.

questions.question: Why is WEP considered very insecure?

options.A: It uses a small static key with the RC4 cipher
options.D: It sends a new key per packet

questions.explanation: WEP's small static key with RC4 is easily cracked.

questions.question: EAP is a framework that mainly offers:
questions.explanation: EAP provides dynamic keys and stronger authentication.

questions.question: How does TKIP differ from WEP?

options.B: TKIP uses one key; WEP uses many
options.C: WEP uses a single key for all encryption; TKIP sends a different key with each packet

questions.explanation: WEP uses one key for everything, while TKIP sends a different key with each packet.

questions.question: AES-CCMP is required with:
questions.explanation: WPA2 requires AES-CCMP.

questions.question: Which is the correct order from weakest to strongest?

options.A: MAC filter < WEP < WPA < WPA2 < WPA3

questions.explanation: Security improves in the order MAC filter, WEP, WPA, WPA2 and WPA3.

questions.question: WPA3 supports key sizes of:
questions.explanation: WPA3 supports 128-bit and 256-bit keys.

questions.question: Which release years are correct for WPA and WPA2?
questions.explanation: WPA was released in 2003 and WPA2 in 2004.

questions.question: A stream cipher such as RC4 works by:

options.A: Encrypting fixed blocks of 64 bits only
options.C: Generating a key stream and combining (XOR) it with the message
options.D: Sending the message in plain text

questions.explanation: A stream cipher generates a key stream and XORs it with the message.

questions.question: In IoT, which statement is correct?

options.A: Sensors collect data; actuators take actions such as switching a device on or off
options.B: Actuators collect data; sensors switch devices

questions.explanation: Sensors collect data, and actuators perform actions such as switching a device on or off.

questions.question: Which IoT layer is responsible for the transmission of data?
questions.explanation: The data exchange layer transmits data in the IoT architecture.

questions.question: In cloud networking, how are office sites typically connected?

options.D: Using a cloud-based VPN and gateway

questions.explanation: Office sites are typically connected through a cloud-based VPN and gateway.

questions.question: "Improved monitoring and maintenance" as a cloud networking benefit means:

options.C: No need for physical management and full visibility of traffic data

questions.explanation: It means no physical management is needed and traffic data is fully visible.

questions.question: The role of virtualization in cloud networking includes:

options.B: Multiplexing a large-capacity cable into several virtual private network links

questions.explanation: Virtualization multiplexes a large-capacity cable into several virtual private network links.

questions.question: A disadvantage of virtual networks is:

options.A: Possible performance limits in latency and bandwidth compared with physical networks

questions.explanation: Virtual networks may have performance limits in latency and bandwidth compared with physical networks.

questions.question: In NFV, which statement is correct?

options.A: Physical devices are added for every function
options.D: Virtual services replace physical devices and a VMM can manage them from the hypervisor

questions.explanation: NFV replaces physical devices with virtual services that a VMM can manage from the hypervisor.

questions.question: If a port group has no mapping to an uplink, the VMs in it can:

options.D: Not communicate at all, even internally

questions.explanation: Without an uplink, the VMs can talk only to each other inside the host.

questions.question: In VMware networking, uplinks are:

options.A: The physical network adapter ports of the hypervisor host

questions.explanation: Uplinks are the physical network adapter ports of the hypervisor host.

questions.question: Which is the correct flow of traffic in VMware virtual networking?

options.B: VM → vNIC → port group → vSwitch → uplink → physical network

questions.explanation: Traffic goes from the VM through its vNIC, port group, vSwitch and uplink to the physical network.

questions.question: The mapping between port groups and uplinks is done at the:
questions.explanation: The vSwitch maps port groups to uplinks.

questions.question: Uplinks can be grouped for redundancy or teaming using:
questions.explanation: Uplinks are grouped for redundancy or teaming using Link Aggregation Groups.

questions.question: In an enterprise design, wireless LAN controllers (WLCs) are placed in the:
questions.explanation: WLCs are placed in the Network Services block.

questions.question: How does virtualization support sustainable (green) computing?

options.A: By increasing the number of physical servers
options.B: By reducing the number of physical servers and energy use
options.C: By removing the need for data centers

questions.explanation: Virtualization reduces the number of physical servers and the energy they use.
